title: How Data Is Stored in Memory

cards.prompt: Order from fastest to slowest storage:
cards.answer: Registers, then SRAM caches, then DRAM, then SSD/HDD.

cards.prompt: What is the typical size and access time of L1 cache?
What does DRAM use to store a bit?
Explain like I'm 10: Why is CPU cache expensive?
cards.answer: Each bit needs several tiny switches (transistors), so a lot of cache costs a lot of space and money.

cards.prompt: Caches are a type of ____ memory.
L2 cache is smaller but faster than L1.
cards.answer: Myth: L2 is bigger (about 256KB-1MB) but slightly slower.

cards.prompt: Why does a computer have caches and RAM instead of just one huge fast memory?
cards.answer: Fast memory like SRAM is costly and small; layering trades speed for capacity and cost, with cache bridging CPU and RAM.
